steps.tx: An **internal jugular** central venous catheter is placed under **ultrasound**. The wire is seen in the vein before any **dilator** is passed. If a large dilator has already entered the carotid artery, it is not pulled out on the ward. That hole is a surgical repair.

vis.alt: Catheter tip at a central vein junction, with unnamed device types and a blockage.
vis.caption: The useful part is the tip sitting at the superior vena cava to right atrium junction. The labels Device Type A and Device Type B are unnamed, so they are not a recommendation. The drawing does not show ultrasound of the wire, or a dilator in the carotid. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.tx: The **3SITES** trial found a lower composite of bloodstream infection and symptomatic thrombosis with the **subclavian** vein than with the jugular or femoral vein, at the cost of more **pneumothorax**. A patient with bad clotting is given a vein that can be compressed. The trial is a default, and it is not a site that ignores the lungs.

right.title: When not to follow it
points: Bad clotting needs a compressible vein
Severe lung disease may change the site
The trial is not blind to the pleura

steps.tx: A radial **arterial cannula** is transduced at the **phlebostatic axis**, the 4th intercostal space at the mid thorax. A dampened trace is an underestimate of the systolic pressure. The **Allen test** does not reliably predict hand ischaemia, and it does not delay the line in an unstable patient.

rows: The test does not delay the line

steps.tx: **Percutaneous dilatational tracheostomy** is elective, it is guided by **bronchoscopy**, and it is sited between tracheal ring 2 and ring 4. It is not made through the cricoid, and it is not an emergency airway. Coagulopathy and very high ventilator pressures are a higher risk. The same bronchoscopy can clear a mucus plug, and the airway is kept secure.

nodes.label: Ring 2 to ring 4, not the cricoid
Defer if clotting or ventilator pressure is extreme

steps.tx: A chest drain is placed in the **triangle of safety**, just above a rib, after a finger sweep, and it is put on an **underwater seal**. A bubbling drain is never clamped, and a tube that has slipped out is not pushed back in. **Needle decompression** of tension is the 4th or 5th intercostal space in the anterior axillary line. The 2nd intercostal space, midclavicular, is an alternative, and a short needle can fail in a thick chest, so a drain follows.

rows: Triangle of safety, above the rib
Underwater, never clamp a bubbling drain

steps.tx: **Lumbar puncture** is avoided when a mass is causing **midline shift**, when the skin is infected, or when a coagulopathy is uncorrected. **Opening pressure** is measured with the patient lateral. A postural headache afterwards is not meningitis, unless fever or a falling conscious level is also present.

vis.alt: A lumbar puncture safety box listing an INR threshold and a platelet threshold.
vis.caption: The chart puts an INR below 1.5 and platelets above 50,000 into a box labelled Safety. Those are common local thresholds, not a guarantee and not the paracentesis rule. They do not override midline shift. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.tx: **Pericardiocentesis** for **tamponade** is guided by echocardiography. In cardiac arrest the approach is subxiphoid. Blood from a cardiac chamber is blood that clots in the bowl, and blood that has sat in the pericardium often does not. **Pulsus paradoxus**, distended neck veins, and chamber collapse are support for the diagnosis before the needle goes in.

left.title: Blood that clots in the bowl
points: The needle is in the heart

steps.tx: Diagnostic **paracentesis** in cirrhosis is not delayed for a moderately raised INR, because missing infected ascites is more dangerous than the tap. When more than 5 litres are removed, **albumin** is given at about 6 to 8 g per litre removed. The central-line bundle is a separate rule: **chlorhexidine** skin preparation and a **maximal sterile barrier**, and it is listed beside the tap rule so the two are not mixed.
